display_title: Roll outer bitonic sort loops with scf.for and deduplicate kernels

head_commit.message:
Roll outer bitonic sort loops with scf.for and deduplicate kernels

Unrolling every bitonic sort mask in C++ produced large kernels with high
register pressure and slow compilation for wide tiles, while rolling all masks
into nested `scf.for` loops introduced dynamic mask bit-scatter and prevented
sub-word/64-bit coalescing on the smallest xor masks. Compiling identical outer
stage kernels multiple times also wasted compilation time.

Keep the outer stage loop and inter-warp step loop rolled with `scf.for` while
unrolling the intra-warp tail masks (`xor_mask` < 64, up to 6 inner steps) and
full-tile intra-tile merge loops in C++, split non-power-of-2 multi-tile
kernels once on the trailing partial tile so full tiles skip bounds checks and
divergence while partial tiles stay rolled with reduced active stages, prevent
`OptimizeLoopsPass` from unrolling loops containing `SyncThreadsOp`, compute
pair indices with bitwise operations instead of division and modulo, and
deduplicate identical kernels using shared cubin buffers.

On B200 sort/topk microbenchmarks (2,014 invocations with sort/topk rewriters
disabled), total compile time improves 1.92x geomean (up to 37x on large
shapes) at 1.00x geomean Wall Time and Device Time. Multi-tile non-power-of-2
shapes (1.02x-1.04x Device Time), high-batch grids (up to 1.08x), and large
sorts speed up via higher SM occupancy (<= 32 regs), while unsaturated grids
(<= 1 CTA/SM on 4096/16384) trade ~1-2 us (0.94x-0.98x) for rolled indexing.

display_title: [XLA] Use TransposePlan::Options::tile_padding in TiledLinearizer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use TransposePlan::Options::tile_padding in TiledLinearizer.

Pass `tile_padding` to `TransposePlan` in `TiledLinearizer::CreateChunkedTransposePlan` and `TiledLinearizer::LinearizeUsingTransposeInto` so `TransposePlan` initializes only the actual padding bytes in parallel instead of pre-filling entire H2D staging slots or linearized destination buffers upfront.

Unify NaN tile padding on `0xff` (`0xffffffff`) to match `RepackToHardwareLayout`, since an all-ones bit pattern is a quiet NaN for IEEE/OCP float types with NaN (`F32`, `F16`, `BF16`, `F8E5M2`, `F8E4M3FN`, etc.) and can be filled with a single repeated byte.

display_title: Hide spdlog namespace instead of renaming via macro

head_commit.message:
Hide spdlog namespace instead of renaming via macro

Defining `spdlog=xla_spdlog` in `@spdlog`'s `defines` propagates `-Dspdlog=xla_spdlog` to all transitive dependents, which rewrites any identifier token named `spdlog` in headers and sources included by those targets.

Since `@spdlog` is a header-only library linked statically into XLA's targets, the symbol collision with `librocroller.so` only happens through the dynamic symbol table. So this change replaces the preprocessor macro with hidden visibility on `namespace spdlog`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Store runtime metadata in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Store runtime metadata in GpuExecutable

`GpuExecutable` read the runtime `DebugOptions`, the `partition_size` and the
static device assignment from the `HloModuleConfig` of its `HloModule`. Without
a module it silently fell back to hard-coded values. That ties execution to the
module, which we want to stop building for loaded executables.

So this change stores the debug options and the static device assignment in
`GpuExecutable` instead. For JIT compiled executables they come from the module
config, and `FromProto` reads them straight from `hlo_module_with_config.config`
(including the fallback to `HloModuleProto.device_assignment` that
`HloModule::CreateFromProto` does). The execution path, the buffer allocator,
the module annotations and the static device assignment check now use the
stored values. The per-flag precedence between compile-time and load-time
options is unchanged and now documented next to the new members.

`CommandBufferConversionPass` now gets the slice size explicitly. It comes from
the `GpuTopology` of the executable, which is also where the compiler takes the
`partition_size` from. Executables serialized before `GpuExecutableProto` had a
`gpu_topology` don't have a topology, so for those we still use the serialized
`partition_size`.

The stored options are a copy taken in `GpuExecutable::Create`, while before
every execution read the live module config. I found no code that changes the
debug options of an executable's module after `Create`, so this doesn't change
anything in practice.

Executables without a module config behave differently now. They ran without
any debug options, so the execution code fell back to hard-coded values. Most of
them match the flag defaults, but one doesn't: without options the communication
streams didn't get the highest priority, while
`xla_gpu_enable_highest_priority_async_stream` defaults to true. Now these
executables use the options passed to `GpuExecutable::Create`. So they get
highest-priority communication streams, and runtime flags set by the user (e.g.
NCCL channels or rendezvous timeouts) take effect for them, like they already do
for executables with a module. That affects two paths:

1. JIT compilation with `xla_embed_hlo_module=false`, where `GpuCompiler`
   passes the compile-time options of the module.
2. `GpuExecutable::FromProto` with a proto without `hlo_module_with_config`
   (which is what such an executable serializes to), where these are the
   load-time options.

Executables with a module behave as before.

Also remove the unused `module_id` parameter of `ExecuteThunksImpl`, and pass
the debug options as a reference, since they are never null anymore.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Flatten WeightedPicker tree into a single heap array.

head_commit.message:
Flatten WeightedPicker tree into a single heap array.

`WeightedPicker` allocated `num_levels_` separate heap arrays (`new int32*[num_levels_]` plus one array per tree level), incurring `num_levels_ + 1` allocations and deallocations on construction, destruction, and resize while pointer-chasing across levels on every `PickAt` and `set_weight` call.

Store all internal nodes and leaves in a single 1-indexed binary heap array of size `1 << num_levels_`, eliminating per-level pointer indirection and cutting tree allocation to a single block.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Synchronize single-block phases via block barriers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Synchronize single-block phases via block barriers.

`PhasedBlockClusterFusion` previously emitted a cluster barrier at every phase boundary and configured even pure single-block fusions as 1-block thread-block clusters. When consecutive phases each execute on a single block (`bid == 0`), cluster barriers pay unnecessary GPC barrier latency and flush SM L1 cache lines that would otherwise stay hot across phases.

Group contiguous runs of single-block phases under a shared `bid < 1` guard and synchronize transitions between single-block phases with a block barrier outside any thread-count guard. When every phase in the fusion uses a single block, omit cluster launch dimensions so the kernel launches without a thread-block cluster.

display_title: PR #52513: [XLA] Reject index_vector_dim as a gather/scatter batching dim

head_commit.message:
PR #52513: [XLA] Reject index_vector_dim as a gather/scatter batching dim

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52513

#ai-generated

**Status quo**: `ValidateGatherDimensionNumbers` (`xla/service/shape_inference.cc:4406`) and `ValidateScatterDimensionNumbers` (`xla/service/shape_inference.cc:4723`) check each start indices (gather) or scatter indices (scatter) batching dim against the indices shape with the implicit trailing index vector dim appended (`ShapeInference::InferGatherShape` and `ShapeInference::InferScatterShape` build that shape before they call the validators). The batching dim loops are at `xla/service/shape_inference.cc:4537` and `xla/service/shape_inference.cc:4848`. They do not reject an entry equal to `index_vector_dim`. The StableHLO spec forbids it (gather C15 and scatter C16: index_vector_dim must not be one of the indices batching dims). So a module that passes the HLO verifier can name the index vector dim as a batching dim, either an explicit `index_vector_dim` or the implicit one that equals the indices rank.

Code that maps batching dims while skipping `index_vector_dim` (`GenerateExplicitBatchDimIndices` at `xla/service/gather_scatter_utils.cc:65`, and `GetStartIndicesDimToOutputDimForExplicitBatchingDims`) does not expect this.

**Why**: Modules of this shape were run through three consumers on the unmodified tree, each parsed with `ParseAndReturnVerifiedModule`, clang 21, `-c opt`, AddressSanitizer and release builds:

| consumer | AddressSanitizer build | release build |
|---|---|---|
| gather expander and scatter expander (explicit and implicit form) | SEGV READ at address 0x58 in `HloInstruction::shape()`, called from `MakeBroadcastHlo` (xla/service/hlo_creation_utils.cc line 282) | SIGSEGV |
| algebraic simplifier gather(pad) rewrite, implicit form | heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 in `CheckPaddedDimsForGatherOfPad` | SIGSEGV |
| algebraic simplifier gather(pad) rewrite, explicit form | uncaught C++ exception from an absl hash map at() lookup | same |

With this change the same modules fail verification with the new error instead. The reproducers are HLO text; no module produced by a frontend (JAX, StableHLO) was tested.

**Design choices**: Both validators return `InvalidArgument` when a batching dim equals `index_vector_dim`. One check per validator covers the explicit and the implicit form, because the implicit index vector dim is already part of the expanded indices shape that the validators receive. No consumer is changed.

**Trade-offs / Alternatives**: A module that names the index vector dim as a batching dim no longer verifies. The spec already forbids such a module. The alternative is to guard each consumer separately, which leaves the relationship accepted for every consumer that is not guarded. The HLO evaluator and the batched gather/scatter normalizer also consume these dimension numbers and were not run on such modules.

**Testing**: Added to `xla/service/shape_inference_test.cc`, for gather (`GatherShapeInferenceTest`) and for scatter (`ScatterShapeInferenceTest`, both parameter sets):

- `BatchingDimEqualToExplicitIndexVectorDim` and `BatchingDimEqualToImplicitIndexVectorDim` (rejected, with the new message)
- `LastRealStartIndicesBatchingDimAccepted` and `LastRealScatterIndicesBatchingDimAccepted` (control: the last real indices dim with an implicit index vector dim)
- `BatchingDimBeforeExplicitIndexVectorDim` and `BatchingDimAfterIndexVectorDim` (controls)

On the unmodified code the rejection tests fail (the call succeeds, 6 failures across gather and both scatter parameter sets) and the controls pass. With the change, the full `//xla/service:shape_inference_test` suite (606 tests, no filter) passes in both an AddressSanitizer build and a release build, and so do the full hlo verifier, hlo parser, hlo evaluator, batched gather/scatter normalizer, gather expander, scatter expander and algebraic simplifier test suites in the AddressSanitizer build. Removing either check makes the matching rejection tests fail, and changing either `==` to `>=` makes the matching "after" control fail.

AI assistance was used in drafting and validating this change; the patch and tests were reviewed and verified by the author.

Copybara import of the project:

--

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Estimate shared memory usage and filter tilings exceeding 50% of shared memory.

Estimate per-block shared memory usage for tiled fusions as the maximum of:
- the largest transpose tile in bytes, and
- the largest cross-warp reduction output tile in bytes (when the reduced dimension tile size exceeds the warp size) multiplied by the number of warps per block.

Reject candidate tilings whose estimated shared memory usage exceeds 50% of the per-block shared memory limit so that at least two thread blocks can co-reside per SM to hide cross-warp synchronization latency.

display_title: PR #49580: [XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

head_commit.message:
PR #49580: [XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49580

📝 Summary of Changes
#ai_generated (but it's been in use internally for several weeks)

When XLA:CPU reduces a large array, it first splits the reduction into a reduce-window that produces partial sums and a smaller reduce over those. The fusion pass knows how to *fuse producers into a reduce*, but not into a *reduce-window*. So in something like `sum(x * y)`, the multiply generates its own loop and writes its entire result to memory, which is read immediately after by the reduce (instead of performing a more optimal loop fusion).

The actual fix is adding `kReduceWindow` to `CanBeLoopFused`, which is one line. I also had to teach `ReusesOperandElements` that a reduce-window with non-overlapping windows touches each input element only once, *as is already done for reduce*.

🎯 Justification

This affects every large reduction that doesn't go to YNNPACK. I ran into it while looking into #49131.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

```
ENTRY main {
  x = bf16[64,1048576] parameter(0)
  y = bf16[64,1048576] parameter(1)
  m = bf16[64,1048576] multiply(x, y)
  c = bf16[] constant(0)
  ROOT r = bf16[64] reduce(m, c), dimensions={1}, to_apply=add
}
```

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| bf16 (above) | 78.0 ms | 28.8 ms |
| same in s32 | 77.7 ms | 12.7 ms |

I didn't see any changes outside the noise on the other CPU benchmarks.

🧪 Unit Tests:

New tests in `hlo_instruction_test` check that a reduce-window reuses elements only when its windows overlap. In `cpu_instruction_fusion_test`, one test fuses a multiply into a non-overlapping reduce-window and another checks that `exp` stays out of an overlapping one.

There was also an existing test in `cpu_fusion_test` that used reduce-window as its example of an op that can't be fused, which is no longer true, so I switched it to sort.
Copybara import of the project:

--
1557a803471eab5d9fe3a3b9b2788b259150452b by jurasic <jurasic@proximafusion.com>:

[XLA:CPU] Allow fusing into kReduceWindow

TreeReductionRewriter splits large reductions into a reduce-window followed by
a reduce. CPU fusion did not accept kReduceWindow, so the input of the
reduce-window was always materialized.

Allow fusing producers into a reduce-window if its windows do not overlap and
are not dilated, so every input element is read once. A reduce-window is never
fused into its consumer. Make ReusesOperandElements return false for the array
operands of such a reduce-window, as it already does for kReduce. Also treat a
max reduce-window like a max reduce when looking for the softmax shift pattern.

Merging this change closes #49580

display_title: Flatten WeightedPicker tree into a single heap array.

head_commit.message:
Flatten WeightedPicker tree into a single heap array.

`WeightedPicker` allocated `num_levels_` separate heap arrays (`new int32*[num_levels_]` plus one array per tree level), incurring `num_levels_ + 1` allocations and deallocations on construction, destruction, and resize while pointer-chasing across levels on every `PickAt` and `set_weight` call.

Store all internal nodes and leaves in a single 1-indexed binary heap array of size `1 << num_levels_`, eliminating per-level pointer indirection and cutting tree allocation to a single block.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015486136

display_title: [XLA] Split stacked MoveToHost dynamic-update-slices in HostOffloadLegalize.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Split stacked MoveToHost dynamic-update-slices in HostOffloadLegalize.

When `jax.lax.scan(..., unroll > 1)` stacks `MoveToHost`-annotated outputs from each unrolled body iteration, it lowers to `MoveToHost -> bitcast -> concatenate` (or `TpuConcatDecomposer` `pad + maximum/add/or` tree) `-> bitcast -> dynamic-update-slice` into the scan output buffer. Because `HostOffloader` only recognizes `MoveToHost` feeding `dynamic-update-slice` through unary bitcast/reshape/copy instructions, it treated the intermediate `concatenate` / `pad+maximum` and `dynamic-update-slice` as host compute (`_xla_compute_type="host"`), which lowered to synchronous CPU `host-call`s.

Decompose a `dynamic-update-slice` whose update operand is a concatenation (or `pad + maximum/add/or` tree) of `MoveToHost` slices into sequential per-slice `dynamic-update-slice` instructions in `HostOffloadLegalize` so each `MoveToHost` feeds its own `dynamic-update-slice` directly and lowers to an asynchronous host DMA.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015605975

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Clear dynamic slice configs in autotuning candidates.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Clear dynamic slice configs in autotuning candidates.

`DynamicSliceAnnotator` annotates dynamic slices with a `DynamicSliceConfig`
that lets the runtime compute the slice offset from the iteration of the
enclosing while loop (or a static offset) instead of the offset operands. When
the autotuner extracts an instruction into a standalone module, that loop no
longer exists and the offset operands are synthetic, so the runtime silently
uses iteration 0 and ignores the offset operands. For a Triton GEMM fusion with
a fused per-layer weight `dynamic-slice`, the cuBLASLt fission reference
therefore always reads the first slice while the Triton candidates read the
slice selected by the (randomly initialized) offset operand. All Triton configs
are then rejected as wrong results, and every rejection produces an expensive
host-side diff report.

Clear all `DynamicSliceConfig`s in the module that `GpuCodegenBackend::Compile`
builds for each candidate. Static configs are cleared as well, because an
offset that is constant in the original module (e.g. in a loop with a single
iteration) can still come from an operand that is a parameter of the extracted
module. The original module, e.g. via `FissionBackend::ApplyConfig`, is
unchanged.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/52255

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014687114

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Build one CppGen bitcode per source

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Build one CppGen bitcode per source

### Status quo

`eigen_unary.cc` (atan) is compiled into three bitcode variants (16, 32 and
64-byte vectors) and `expm1.cc` into two. `GetCppGenLibraries` picks one per
target from the CPU features and preferred vector width.

Since atan stopped using Eigen, all variants contain the same function bodies.
The only difference is that SysV x86 builds without AVX-512 pass 512-bit
vectors through a `byval` pointer, which `CreateDirectAdapter` already adapts
and the inliner removes.

### Why

The variants cost build targets, embedded binary size and selection code
without changing the generated kernels. The Eigen names and build flags left
behind are misleading.

### Changes

*   Build `atan_ll` and `expm1_ll` once, with no per-width copts or
    `-mavx512f`. Remove `GetCppGenIrString`, `SelectIrString` and
    `AreEigenIntrinsicsAvailable`.
*   Rename `eigen_unary.{h,cc}` to `atan.{h,cc}` and `EigenAtan` to `Atan`,
    matching `Expm1`, `Sin` and `Cos`. Delete the unregistered `EigenTanh`.
*   Drop the Eigen include and `ArrayMap` from `vector_ops.h`, and
    `-DEIGEN_VECTORIZE_GENERIC` from `cc_to_llvm_ir.bzl`.
*   Collapse the per-width tests onto the single bitcode.
    `AtanHasNoLibmCallsAfterInlining` replaces
    `DefinesAvxAndAvx512EigenAtanF64` and covers every f32 and f64 width on
    AVX2 and AVX-512.

### Verification

Kernel IR after `DefineIntrinsicFunctions` + `RunInlineAndOptPasses` is
byte-identical for every atan and expm1 width on SSE4.2, AVX2 and AVX-512
(512- and 256-bit preference), except the 512-bit widths on AVX-512, which now
go through the adapter. Those have the same instructions, with a dropped
`noundef` on one `fabs` call and two independent bitcasts in swapped order.

### Alternatives

*   Keep the variants and only rename: smaller diff, but keeps the dead
    selection logic.
*   Keep one variant per ABI to avoid `byval` adaptation: AArch64 passes
    512-bit vectors indirectly too, so the adapter stays either way, and it
    costs nothing after inlining.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017278135

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add MultiPhaseFusion pass.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add MultiPhaseFusion pass.

Dependent small fusions execute as separate kernels dominated by fixed launch and scheduling overheads. Grouping them into nested `__phased_block_cluster` fusions lowered by `PhasedBlockClusterFusion` executes them as sequential phases of a single thread-block-cluster kernel separated by cluster barriers, paying launch overhead once while exchanging intermediate results via DRAM or caches.

Current limitations (to be lifted in follow-up CLs):

* Greedily forms straight-line producer-consumer chains
* Only `kLoop` stages whose 1D grid fits a single thread-block cluster

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017277442

display_title: [XLA] Use TransposePlan::Options::tile_padding in TiledLinearizer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use TransposePlan::Options::tile_padding in TiledLinearizer.

Pass `tile_padding` to `TransposePlan` in `TiledLinearizer::CreateChunkedTransposePlan` and `TiledLinearizer::LinearizeUsingTransposeInto` so `TransposePlan` initializes only the actual padding bytes in parallel instead of pre-filling entire H2D staging slots or linearized destination buffers upfront.

Unify NaN tile padding on `0xff` (`0xffffffff`) to match `RepackToHardwareLayout`, since an all-ones bit pattern is a quiet NaN for IEEE/OCP float types with NaN (`F32`, `F16`, `BF16`, `F8E5M2`, `F8E4M3FN`, etc.) and can be filled with a single repeated byte.

head_commit.message:
PR #52537: [XLA:CPU] Add PowerPC support to XLA CPU intrinsic device detection

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52537

Description:
#ai-generated

📝 Summary of Changes
Map PowerPC target triples to a new `DeviceType::kPowerPcCpu` in `IrCompiler`
instead of hitting `LOG(FATAL)`, and link the cpp-gen intrinsic libraries for
it, as is done for SystemZ (#36482, 55c3e230dab2).

🎯 Justification
On a PowerPC host every XLA:CPU compilation aborts:

    ir_compiler.cc:423] Unsupported CPU type: powerpc64le-unknown-freebsd

Found with jaxlib 0.12.0.1 on FreeBSD/powerpc64le: the wheel builds, but the
first `jax.jit` call kills the process. The check only looks at the
architecture, so Linux ppc64le is affected too. The cpp-gen libraries are
needed because `ElementalIrEmitter::EmitExpm1` always emits `xla.expm1.*`
calls, and `GetCppGenFunction` CHECK-fails if no library defines them.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:
None, as in #36482: the PowerPC LLVM backend is only linked for
`//xla/tsl:ppc64le_or_cross`, so CI hosts cannot create a PowerPC target
machine.

🧪 Execution Tests:
FreeBSD 15.1/powerpc64le (POWER9), jaxlib 0.12.0.1 built from source (XLA
d867969800d4) with this change. That snapshot predates 3af77b5776fb, so its
expm1.cc guard change was backported as well: clang does not define
`__FLT16_MANT_DIG__` on PowerPC, so the old guard left the expm1 IR library
empty.
- Before: the first `jax.jit` call aborts with the error above.
- After: jitted expm1, atan, tanh, exp, log1p, sinh, cosh, sin, cos and rsqrt
  on F32 and F64 (rtol 2e-5 and 1e-12), erf on F32 and tanh on C64 match
  NumPy/SciPy.
Copybara import of the project:

Add PowerPC support to XLA CPU intrinsic device detection

#ai-generated

IrCompiler::RunIrPasses maps the target triple to an intrinsics
DeviceType and hits LOG(FATAL) for anything other than x86, ARM and
SystemZ, so every XLA:CPU compilation on a PowerPC host aborts with

  Unsupported CPU type: powerpc64le-unknown-freebsd

This was found running jaxlib on FreeBSD/powerpc64le. The check only

display_title: Roll outer bitonic sort loops with scf.for and deduplicate kernels

head_commit.message:
Roll outer bitonic sort loops with scf.for and deduplicate kernels

Unrolling every bitonic sort mask in C++ produced large kernels with high
register pressure and slow compilation for wide tiles, while rolling all masks
into nested `scf.for` loops introduced dynamic mask bit-scatter and prevented
sub-word/64-bit coalescing on the smallest xor masks. Compiling identical outer
stage kernels multiple times also wasted compilation time.

Keep the outer stage loop and inter-warp step loop rolled with `scf.for` while
unrolling the intra-warp tail masks (`xor_mask` < 64, up to 6 inner steps) and
full-tile intra-tile merge loops in C++, split non-power-of-2 multi-tile
kernels once on the trailing partial tile so full tiles skip bounds checks and
divergence while partial tiles stay rolled with reduced active stages, prevent
`OptimizeLoopsPass` from unrolling loops containing `SyncThreadsOp`, compute
pair indices with bitwise operations instead of division and modulo, and
deduplicate identical kernels using shared cubin buffers.

On B200 sort/topk microbenchmarks (2,014 invocations with sort/topk rewriters
disabled), total compile time improves 1.92x geomean (up to 37x on large
shapes) at 1.00x geomean Wall Time and Device Time. Multi-tile non-power-of-2
shapes (1.02x-1.04x Device Time), high-batch grids (up to 1.08x), and large
sorts speed up via higher SM occupancy (<= 32 regs), while unsaturated grids
(<= 1 CTA/SM on 4096/16384) trade ~1-2 us (0.94x-0.98x) for rolled indexing.

display_title: Hide spdlog namespace instead of renaming via macro

head_commit.message:
Hide spdlog namespace instead of renaming via macro

Defining `spdlog=xla_spdlog` in `@spdlog`'s `defines` propagates `-Dspdlog=xla_spdlog` to all transitive dependents, which rewrites any identifier token named `spdlog` in headers and sources included by those targets.

Since `@spdlog` is a header-only library linked statically into XLA's targets, the symbol collision with `librocroller.so` only happens through the dynamic symbol table. So this change replaces the preprocessor macro with hidden visibility on `namespace spdlog`.

display_title: Store runtime metadata in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Store runtime metadata in GpuExecutable

`GpuExecutable` read the runtime `DebugOptions`, the `partition_size` and the
static device assignment from the `HloModuleConfig` of its `HloModule`. Without
a module it silently fell back to hard-coded values. That ties execution to the
module, which we want to stop building for loaded executables.

So this change stores the debug options and the static device assignment in
`GpuExecutable` instead. For JIT compiled executables they come from the module
config, and `FromProto` reads them straight from `hlo_module_with_config.config`
(including the fallback to `HloModuleProto.device_assignment` that
`HloModule::CreateFromProto` does). The execution path, the buffer allocator,
the module annotations and the static device assignment check now use the
stored values. The per-flag precedence between compile-time and load-time
options is unchanged and now documented next to the new members.

`CommandBufferConversionPass` now gets the slice size explicitly. It comes from
the `GpuTopology` of the executable, which is also where the compiler takes the
`partition_size` from. Executables serialized before `GpuExecutableProto` had a
`gpu_topology` don't have a topology, so for those we still use the serialized
`partition_size`.

The stored options are a copy taken in `GpuExecutable::Create`, while before
every execution read the live module config. I found no code that changes the
debug options of an executable's module after `Create`, so this doesn't change
anything in practice.

Executables without a module config behave differently now. They ran without
any debug options, so the execution code fell back to hard-coded values. Most of
them match the flag defaults, but one doesn't: without options the communication
streams didn't get the highest priority, while
`xla_gpu_enable_highest_priority_async_stream` defaults to true. Now these
executables use the options passed to `GpuExecutable::Create`. So they get
highest-priority communication streams, and runtime flags set by the user (e.g.
NCCL channels or rendezvous timeouts) take effect for them, like they already do
for executables with a module. That affects two paths:

1. JIT compilation with `xla_embed_hlo_module=false`, where `GpuCompiler`
   passes the compile-time options of the module.
2. `GpuExecutable::FromProto` with a proto without `hlo_module_with_config`
   (which is what such an executable serializes to), where these are the
   load-time options.

Executables with a module behave as before.

Also remove the unused `module_id` parameter of `ExecuteThunksImpl`, and pass
the debug options as a reference, since they are never null anymore.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add MultiPhaseFusion pass.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add MultiPhaseFusion pass.

Dependent small fusions execute as separate kernels dominated by fixed launch and scheduling overheads. Grouping them into nested `__phased_block_cluster` fusions lowered by `PhasedBlockClusterFusion` executes them as sequential phases of a single thread-block-cluster kernel separated by cluster barriers, paying launch overhead once while exchanging intermediate results via DRAM or caches.

Current limitations (to be lifted in follow-up CLs):

* Greedily forms straight-line producer-consumer chains
* Only `kLoop` stages whose 1D grid fits a single thread-block cluster

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Roll outer bitonic sort loops with scf.for and deduplicate kernels

head_commit.message:
Roll outer bitonic sort loops with scf.for and deduplicate kernels

Unrolling every bitonic sort mask in C++ produced large kernels with high
register pressure and slow compilation for wide tiles, while rolling all masks
into nested `scf.for` loops introduced dynamic mask bit-scatter and prevented
sub-word/64-bit coalescing on the smallest xor masks. Compiling identical outer
stage kernels multiple times also wasted compilation time.

Keep the outer stage loop and inter-warp step loop rolled with `scf.for` while
unrolling the intra-warp tail masks (`xor_mask` < 64, up to 6 inner steps) and
full-tile intra-tile merge loops in C++, split non-power-of-2 multi-tile
kernels once on the trailing partial tile so full tiles skip bounds checks and
divergence while partial tiles stay rolled with reduced active stages, prevent
`OptimizeLoopsPass` from unrolling loops containing `SyncThreadsOp`, compute
pair indices with bitwise operations instead of division and modulo, and
deduplicate identical kernels using shared cubin buffers.

On B200 sort/topk microbenchmarks (2,014 invocations with sort/topk rewriters
disabled), total compile time improves 1.92x geomean (up to 37x on large
shapes) at 1.00x geomean Wall Time and Device Time. Multi-tile non-power-of-2
shapes (1.02x-1.04x Device Time), high-batch grids (up to 1.08x), and large
sorts speed up via higher SM occupancy (<= 32 regs), while unsaturated grids
(<= 1 CTA/SM on 4096/16384) trade ~1-2 us (0.94x-0.98x) for rolled indexing.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Reland: Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in `EstimateNumWarps`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Reland: Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in `EstimateNumWarps`.

`EstimateNumWarps` picks the warp count from the largest padded tile in the fusion. Keep counting operand and root tiles in full, ignore non-root `broadcast` and `constant` tiles, size non-root `iota` by its extent along `iota_dimension`, and scale other non-root array tiles by `min(element_bytes, 4) / 4` so narrow intermediates do not inflate the warp count.

This relands cl/1008957649 (rolled back in cl/1010131399) without the `blocks_per_core` compute-time change that caused the regression.

head_commit.message:
Hide spdlog namespace instead of renaming via macro

Defining `spdlog=xla_spdlog` in `@spdlog`'s `defines` propagates `-Dspdlog=xla_spdlog` to all transitive dependents, which rewrites any identifier token named `spdlog` in headers and sources included by those targets.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Wait on the host for cross-device events before enqueuing D2D copies.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Wait on the host for cross-device events before enqueuing D2D copies.

A D2D copy from GPU 0 to GPU 1 makes GPU 0's stream wait for an event on GPU 1.
If that event is stuck behind a collective on GPU 1 and a context-synchronizing
call (like cuModuleLoad) runs on GPU 0, GPU 0 can never launch its half of the collective, which creates a deadlock.

Waiting for the event asynchronously on the host instead keeps GPU 0's stream free, so GPU 0 can still launch its half of the collective.

The new behavior is off by default and behind `XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_WAIT_CROSS_DEVICE_COPIES=true`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010481212

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add MultiPhaseFusion pass.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add MultiPhaseFusion pass.

Dependent small fusions execute as separate kernels dominated by fixed launch and scheduling overheads. Grouping them into nested `__phased_block_cluster` fusions lowered by `PhasedBlockClusterFusion` executes them as sequential phases of a single thread-block-cluster kernel separated by cluster barriers, paying launch overhead once while exchanging intermediate results via DRAM or caches.

Current limitations (to be lifted in follow-up CLs):

* Greedily forms straight-line producer-consumer chains
* Only `kLoop` stages whose 1D grid fits a single thread-block cluster

Estimate per-block shared memory usage for tiled fusions as the maximum of:

display_title: Harden CheckpointReader, BundleReader, TwoLevelIterator, and Block against read errors and corrupt metadata.

head_commit.message:
Harden CheckpointReader, BundleReader, TwoLevelIterator, and Block against read errors and corrupt metadata.

Previously, transient file read errors (such as `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`) or malformed metadata entries during V2 checkpoint scanning could cause `SIGSEGV` or `SIGABRT` crashes:

- `TwoLevelIterator::Next()`, `key()`, and `value()`, as well as `Block::Iter::Next()`, `key()`, and `value()`, now guard against `!Valid()` instead of dereferencing a null `data_iter_` in release builds.
- `Block::Iter` initializes and resets `value_` to `(data_ + restarts_, 0)` so `NextEntryOffset()` never subtracts `data_` from `nullptr`, validates restart offsets against `restarts_` before forming pointers in `Seek()` and `SeekToRestartPoint()`, and uses 64-bit arithmetic in `DecodeEntry()` to prevent 32-bit unsigned integer overflow when checking `(*non_shared + *value_length)`.
- `BundleReader::status()` now propagates `iter_->status()` when `status_` is OK, and `BundleReader::DebugString()` avoids `CHECK`-crashing on invalid iterator states, unparseable `BundleEntryProto` values, or invalid `TensorShapeProto` entries.
- `CheckpointReader::BuildV2VarMaps()` checks `v2_reader_->Valid()` after `Seek(kHeaderEntryKey)` and `v2_reader_->status()` after each pass, replaces `CHECK(entry.ParseFromString(...))`, `TensorSlice(slice_proto)`, `CHECK(filtered_keys.insert(...).second)`, and `TensorShape(entry.shape())` with status-checked builders (`TensorSlice::BuildTensorSlice` and `TensorShape::BuildTensorShape`), and surfaces `DataLossError` via `TF_Status` when `BuildV2VarMaps()` fails without an underlying reader I/O error.

display_title: Diff PR merge commits against first parent in change_detector and bazel_diff

head_commit.message:
Diff PR merge commits against first parent in change_detector and bazel_diff

On `pull_request` workflows, a PR commit `P` (`head_sha`) is typically branched off an older `main` commit `A` (such as the baseline revision of an exported Copybara CL), while `main` has since advanced to `M` (`base_sha`). When `actions/checkout` runs without an explicit `ref`, it checks out GitHub's synthetic merge commit `S` (`refs/pull/<N>/merge`) as `HEAD`, which merges `P` (`HEAD^2`) into `M` (`HEAD^1`):

```
main:       ... --- A --- (commits on main) --- M (base_sha / HEAD^1)
                     \                           \
PR branch:            \--- P (head_sha / HEAD^2) -+--- S (HEAD, synthetic merge)
```

Previously, `change_detector.py` and `bazel_diff.py` diffed `base_sha` (`M`) against `head_sha` (`P`) using `M...P`, which compares the merge-base `A` against `P`:

1. Finding the merge-base `A` requires fetching git history all the way back from `M` to `A`. When `A` is more than 50 commits behind `M`, `ensure_base_fetched` could not reach `A` within `--depth=50` and fell back to `git fetch --unshallow origin` (~65s overhead).
2. If any commit on `main` between `A` and `M` modified a `.bzl` or Bazel config file, `P` did not contain that upstream change while `S` (`HEAD`) did, so `_has_global_config_skew_from_head` detected a difference between `P` and `S` and forced a full test run.

Since `S` (`HEAD`) already merges `P` (`HEAD^2`) into `M` (`HEAD^1`), the diff between `HEAD^1` (`M`) and `HEAD` (`S`) contains the PR's changes on top of `M`. Therefore this change updates `change_detector.evaluate_skip` and `bazel_diff.compute_impacted_targets` to detect when `HEAD` is a merge commit whose second parent is `head_sha` and rewrite `(base_sha, head_sha)` to `(HEAD^1, HEAD)`. This keeps the shallow fetch 1 commit deep, avoids false config skew from upstream `main` commits, and runs `bazel-diff` on the exact commit trees under test.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017181838

display_title: Diff PR merge commits against first parent in change_detector and bazel_diff

head_commit.message:
Diff PR merge commits against first parent in change_detector and bazel_diff

On `pull_request` workflows, a PR commit `P` (`head_sha`) is typically branched off an older `main` commit `A` (such as the baseline revision of an exported Copybara CL), while `main` has since advanced to `M` (`base_sha`). When `actions/checkout` runs without an explicit `ref`, it checks out GitHub's synthetic merge commit `S` (`refs/pull/<N>/merge`) as `HEAD`, which merges `P` (`HEAD^2`) into `M` (`HEAD^1`):

```
main:       ... --- A --- (commits on main) --- M (base_sha / HEAD^1)
                     \                           \
PR branch:            \--- P (head_sha / HEAD^2) -+--- S (HEAD, synthetic merge)
```

Previously, `change_detector.py` and `bazel_diff.py` diffed `base_sha` (`M`) against `head_sha` (`P`) using `M...P`, which compares the merge-base `A` against `P`:

1. Finding the merge-base `A` requires fetching git history all the way back from `M` to `A`. When `A` is more than 50 commits behind `M`, `ensure_base_fetched` could not reach `A` within `--depth=50` and fell back to `git fetch --unshallow origin` (~65s overhead).
2. If any commit on `main` between `A` and `M` modified a `.bzl` or Bazel config file, `P` did not contain that upstream change while `S` (`HEAD`) did, so `_has_global_config_skew_from_head` detected a difference between `P` and `S` and forced a full test run.

Since `S` (`HEAD`) already merges `P` (`HEAD^2`) into `M` (`HEAD^1`), the diff between `HEAD^1` (`M`) and `HEAD` (`S`) contains the PR's changes on top of `M`. Therefore this change updates `change_detector.evaluate_skip` and `bazel_diff.compute_impacted_targets` to detect when `HEAD` is a merge commit whose second parent is `head_sha` and rewrite `(base_sha, head_sha)` to `(HEAD^1, HEAD)`. This keeps the shallow fetch 1 commit deep, avoids false config skew from upstream `main` commits, and runs `bazel-diff` on the exact commit trees under test.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017181838

[XLA:GPU] Wire up HLO, MLIR, and bytecode dumping in `TensorIrFusion`.

When dumping is enabled for the module and `--xla_dump_emitter_re` matches `tensor-ir-fusion`, dump:

- `<fusion>.hlo`: standalone fusion HLO module.
- `<fusion>.tensor_ir.mlir`: legalized `nv_tensor_ir.graph` module with layout strides, buffer alignments, and the `CompilerInvocation` options header.
- `<fusion>.cuda_tile.mlir`: lowered `cuda_tile` dialect module with `cuda-tile-translate` and `tileiras` command-line headers.
- `<fusion>.tilebc`: serialized CUDA Tile IR bytecode before `tileiras` assembly.

display_title: Hide spdlog namespace instead of renaming via macro

head_commit.message:
Hide spdlog namespace instead of renaming via macro

Defining `spdlog=xla_spdlog` in `@spdlog`'s `defines` propagates `-Dspdlog=xla_spdlog` to all transitive dependents, which rewrites any identifier token named `spdlog` in headers and sources included by those targets.

Since `@spdlog` is a header-only library linked statically into XLA's targets, the symbol collision with `librocroller.so` only happens through the dynamic symbol table. So this change replaces the preprocessor macro with hidden visibility on `namespace spdlog`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017161773

display_title: Previously, `jax.profiler.TraceAnnotation` and `StepTraceAnnotation` only emitted `TraceMe` events, leaving Nsight Systems (`nsys`) and Nsight Compute (`ncu`) without JAX user or step ranges on the NVTX timeline.

head_commit.message:
Previously, `jax.profiler.TraceAnnotation` and `StepTraceAnnotation` only emitted `TraceMe` events, leaving Nsight Systems (`nsys`) and Nsight Compute (`ncu`) without JAX user or step ranges on the NVTX timeline.

Update `TraceMeWrapper` in `xla/python/profiler.cc` to format the label (including `kwargs` metadata such as `step_num`), register it in a bounded cache via `tsl::profiler::RegisterString`, and push/pop an NVTX range on `DefaultProfilerDomain()` when NVTX is active, enabling `nsys --capture-range=nvtx` with negligible overhead when NVTX is not injected.

display_title: [XLA:TPU] Let copy removal elide chained in-place copies of a shared buffer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:TPU] Let copy removal elide chained in-place copies of a shared buffer.

When one loop iteration reads and then updates a loop-carried buffer in place
several times in a row (e.g. gather + scatter optimizer updates of an embedding
table across unrolled loop steps), CopyInsertion adds a copy before every
in-place op and CopyRemover cannot remove any of them: in each step the copy and
the reader of the previous value are unordered, so removing one step's copy
requires the next step's reader to be ordered before the next copy, and vice
versa.

Add an opt-in CopyInsertion option that orders the other readers of an in-place
operand that are already predecessors of the in-place op before the copy added
for that operand. This does not constrain the schedule beyond what the in-place
op already requires, but gives copy removal the ordering it needs. The option is
only enabled for the TPU copy insertion pass for now.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017146632

display_title: PR #52256: Prevent copies in async computations by propagating constraints onto async roots

head_commit.message:
PR #52256: Prevent copies in async computations by propagating constraints onto async roots

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52256

📝 Summary of Changes

`LayoutAssignment` can currently insert copies into async HloComputations that must contain only parameter instructions and a root. This causes the output HLO to fail verification (the HLO verifier requires async computations to contain only parameter instructions and a root).

This PR modifies constraint propagation logic to prevent copies inside async computations. When propagating constraints into async computations, incoming constraints on parameters are redirected to the root's corresponding operands. Incoming constraints on the async computation's result are already attached to the async root. Existing constraint negotiation logic will select a consistent set of constraints for the root. The selected root operand constraints will then propagate mandatorily to the parameters. This ensures that there are no layout mismatches inside the async body, and forces mismatches to be handled by copies before async-start or after async-done.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Cache symmetric memory registrations on communicators.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Cache symmetric memory registrations on communicators.

Previously, `CollectiveMemoryCache` was owned per `GpuExecutable` and keyed by the exact sub-allocation address, preventing symmetric memory windows from being reused across executables sharing a communicator or across sub-slices of the same physical collective arena.
This change moves registration ownership to the GPU communicator instead. Instead of registering one specific buffer allocation, this change queries `StreamExecutor::GetMemoryRange` in `AcquireCollectiveMemory` to register the enclosing physical memory. This works since collective memory space should be symmetrical across all participant devices and it should be allocated from the beginning of the physically allocated arena.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:TPU] Let copy removal elide chained in-place copies of a shared buffer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:TPU] Let copy removal elide chained in-place copies of a shared buffer.

When one loop iteration reads and then updates a loop-carried buffer in place
several times in a row (e.g. gather + scatter optimizer updates of an embedding
table across unrolled loop steps), CopyInsertion adds a copy before every
in-place op and CopyRemover cannot remove any of them: in each step the copy and
the reader of the previous value are unordered, so removing one step's copy
requires the next step's reader to be ordered before the next copy, and vice
versa.

Add an opt-in CopyInsertion option that orders the other readers of an in-place
operand that are already predecessors of the in-place op before the copy added
for that operand. This does not constrain the schedule beyond what the in-place
op already requires, but gives copy removal the ordering it needs. The option is
only enabled for the TPU copy insertion pass for now.

Currently, valid input HLO containing async computations can become invalid during layout assignment, causing subsequent HLO verification to fail compilation. The added tests include HLO that triggers this issue.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

- Added layout-sensitive HLO verification at the end of these existing tests to reject extra instructions inside restricted async bodies and check layout consistency:

  - `AsyncStartDoneMandatoryConstraints`
  - `AsyncStartDoneTupleMandatoryConstraints`
  - `AsyncStartPreservesMandatoryCallerParameterLayout`
  - `AsyncStartPreservesMandatoryCallerParameterLayoutMultipleOperands`
  - `AsyncStartPreservesMandatoryCallerCustomCallLayout`
  - `PropagateAsyncStartConstraintIntoUnconstrainedWrappedComputation`

  The last test also checks that no copies are inserted when the flexible elementwise root can satisfy agreeing caller requirements.

- `AsyncDoneEntryRootLayoutMismatch`: a fixed custom-call result conflicts with the entry result layout; checks that the copy becomes the entry root after async-done.
- `AsyncDoneCallerOperandLayoutMismatch`: a fixed custom-call result conflicts with a caller consumer's operand requirement; checks that the copy is between async-done and that consumer.
- `PropagateAsyncDoneComputationConstraintIntoUnconstrainedWrappedComputation`: a layout requirement on an async-done due to the entry computation layout propagates into the flexible wrapped computation with no copies inserted.
- `PropagateAsyncDoneUseConstraintIntoUnconstrainedWrappedComputation`: a layout requirement on an async-done due to a subsequent use by a custom call propagates into the flexible wrapped computation with no copies inserted.
- `AsyncStartPropagatesLayoutsToReorderedAndRepeatedParameterUses`: distinct caller input layouts propagate to reordered and repeated root operands without copies.
- `AsyncRootOverridesHigherPriorityParameterConstraint`: a test subclass adds a conflicting high-priority parameter constraint; checks that mandatory root-to-parameter propagation replaces it without copies.
- `AsyncComputationWithWhileRoot`: Ensures that modified layout assignment works for a more complicated example where a while op is the root of an async computation.

🧪 Execution Tests

Execution tests with 3 different MaxText recipes across 1–2 GB300 nodes show no meaningful changes in performance or final loss. Furthermore, the HLO after optimization and thunk sequences are identical between baseline and test runs for all three recipes.

The recipes below use the same training args and XLA flags as described [here](https://gist.github.com/rao-ashish/4d01922faf917d7c341c61cdb6a8e3f5). display_title: PR #52481: [ROCm profiler] Keep 64-bit correlation ids when joining activities

head_commit.message:
PR #52481: [ROCm profiler] Keep 64-bit correlation ids when joining activities

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52481

## Problem

`ApiActivityInfoExchange` copies each key of `activity_ops_events_map_` into a `uint32_t corr_id` before looking up the matching HIP API event. openxla/xla#47225 widened correlation ids and these maps to `uint64_t`, the width of `rocprofiler_correlation_id_t::internal`, but missed this local.

For an id at or above 2^32, the lookup uses the truncated value and finds no API event, so every activity row under that id is dropped as "Could not find the counterpart HIP API", and the drop is logged with the truncated id. rocprofiler-sdk hands out internal ids from one process-wide 64-bit counter, so this only shows up after a process has used more than 2^32 ids. I have not seen it in a real trace; the unit test below reproduces it.

## Change

- `const uint32_t corr_id` -> `const uint64_t corr_id` in `ApiActivityInfoExchange`.
- `TestAddKernelEventAndExport` now uses correlation id 2^32 + 42. On the old code the kernel row is dropped and the GPU plane has no lines.

`rocm_collector_test` and `rocm_tracer_test_amdgpu_any` pass on MI355X.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Cache symmetric memory registrations on communicators.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Cache symmetric memory registrations on communicators.

Previously, `CollectiveMemoryCache` was owned per `GpuExecutable` and keyed by the exact sub-allocation address, preventing symmetric memory windows from being reused across executables sharing a communicator or across sub-slices of the same physical collective arena.
This change moves registration ownership to the GPU communicator instead. Instead of registering one specific buffer allocation, this change queries `StreamExecutor::GetMemoryRange` in `AcquireCollectiveMemory` to register the enclosing physical memory. This works since collective memory space should be symmetrical across all participant devices and it should be allocated from the beginning of the physically allocated arena.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007237496

display_title: Add `TraceMeFilter::kTraceHostEnqueueCallback = 1` in `trace_filter_utils.h`, and clear that bit (bit 1, mask `0x2`) in `kTraceMeDefaultFilterMask` in `traceme.h` using a new `kTraceMeHostEnqueueCallbackFilter` constant with the same value. `traceme.h` cannot depend on `trace_filter_utils.h`, so `traceme_recorder_test` checks with a `static_assert` that the two stay equal.

head_commit.message:
Add `TraceMeFilter::kTraceHostEnqueueCallback = 1` in `trace_filter_utils.h`, and clear that bit (bit 1, mask `0x2`) in `kTraceMeDefaultFilterMask` in `traceme.h` using a new `kTraceMeHostEnqueueCallbackFilter` constant with the same value. `traceme.h` cannot depend on `trace_filter_utils.h`, so `traceme_recorder_test` checks with a `static_assert` that the two stay equal.

Sessions configured with `host_traceme_filter_mask = (1ULL << kTraceHostEnqueueCallback)` record only `TraceMe` events tagged with that bit. Sessions without a filter or with the `kTraceMemory` filter record the same events as before, including the tagged ones. `traceme_recorder_test` covers both cases.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1011286453

head_commit.message:
PR #129734: Add tf.experimental.numpy diff prepend/append support with NumPy semantics

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/pull/129734

NumPy's `np.diff` accepts optional `prepend`/`append` values that are added along `axis` before the differences run:

```
>>> np.diff(np.array([1, 2, 3]), prepend=0)
array([1, 1, 1])

>>> np.diff(np.array([1, 2, 3]), append=5)
array([1, 1, 2])
```

The tf-numpy wrapper lacked both parameters entirely: `tnp.diff(a, prepend=0)` raises `TypeError: diff() got an unexpected keyword argument 'prepend'`.

Mirror NumPy's implementation in `np_math_ops.diff`:

- A scalar (0-d) `prepend`/`append` is broadcast to length 1 along `axis` and all other dimensions of `a` (NumPy's `_broadcast_to` on `shape` with `shape[axis] = 1`) and concatenated once, before the `n` differences run.
- An array `prepend`/`append` is concatenated as-is; when both shapes are statically known, a dimension mismatch outside `axis` raises NumPy's exact `ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly` instead of the backend's `InvalidArgumentError`.
- The two sides are promoted to a shared dtype with `np_utils.result_type` before concatenating, like NumPy's concatenate promotes (e.g. `np.diff(int32, prepend=1.5)` yields float64).
- Boolean inputs keep the boolean (`!=`) difference semantics when the promoted dtype is still boolean.

Tests extend `testDiff`: scalar `prepend`/`append` (including `n=2` with both boundaries), array `prepend` with `axis=0` and array `append` with `axis=1` matched against `np.diff`, the mixed-dtype promotion case, the boolean-boundary case, and a mismatch outside `axis` raising NumPy's ValueError.

Signed-off-by: Kaivalya Singh <singh.kaivalya@gmail.com>

display_title: [XLA:GPU] [1/2] Sink reduce through unstrided slice consumers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] [1/2] Sink reduce through unstrided slice consumers.

***Problem:*** When `DotMerger` packs several dots into one and `SplitkRewriter` then splits that dot, the split-K `reduce` feeds unstrided `slice` ops that extract each original dot's result, so it can only be fused into those slices via the slow naive `kLoop` emitter (small split-K) or not at all (large split-K).

***Solution:*** In `GpuAlgebraicSimplifier`, when every consumer of a `reduce` maps to a contiguous unstrided `slice` (optionally through unary elementwise, `bitcast`, or `reshape` ops) and the slices together cover no more elements than the `reduce` output, replace each `slice` chain with a `reduce` over the correspondingly sliced input followed by the replayed passthrough ops so each original dot gets its own reduction without reducing or reading more elements.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1006868296

display_title: [IFRT] Remove redundant `DCHECK(this)` checks in IFRT and PjRt-IFRT

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Remove redundant `DCHECK(this)` checks in IFRT and PjRt-IFRT

In C++, invoking a non-static member function on a null pointer is undefined behavior before the function body executes, allowing compilers to assume `this` is always non-null. As a result, `DCHECK(this)` inside member functions provides no reliable runtime protection and serves only as dead boilerplate.

Remove all remaining `DCHECK(this)` assertions across `xla::ifrt::Sharding`, `xla::ifrt::ShardingSpec`, IFRT IR loaded executables, and PjRt-IFRT client, array, executable, compiler, tuple, and string-array implementations. Also prune the resulting unused includes and build dependencies.

display_title: Replace `PjRtRawBuffer::GetExternalDmaInfo()` with `AcquireExternalDmaAccess()`.

head_commit.message:
Replace `PjRtRawBuffer::GetExternalDmaInfo()` with `AcquireExternalDmaAccess()`.

`GetExternalDmaInfo()` (cl/1008163882) returns a raw buffer's offset and size
inside the backend's dma-buf, for external DMA engines such as NICs. Because
it is a one-shot query, PJRT never learns when the external engine is done
with that address. On TPU, HBM compaction can move an allocation whenever no
TPU DMA is using it; without knowing about the external DMA, compaction can
move the buffer out from under the NIC.

`AcquireExternalDmaAccess()` fixes this by returning a ref-counted handle
instead of the raw address:

```c++
class ExternalDmaAccess {
  virtual ~ExternalDmaAccess() = default;  // subclasses unpin here
  const ExternalDmaInfo& info() const;
};
virtual tsl::AsyncValueRef<ExternalDmaAccess> AcquireExternalDmaAccess();
```

The `AsyncValueRef` resolves once the buffer is allocated and its address is
fixed, and the access ends when the caller drops the last reference. A
follow-up CL implements this in `TpuRawBuffer` by pinning the HBM range
against compaction until `~ExternalDmaAccess()` runs.

On the C API side, `get_external_dma_info` (the last slot, no callers yet) is
replaced in place by `acquire_external_dma_access`, which returns a
`PJRT_ExternalDmaAccess` struct `{vtable, PJRT_DeviceEvent}`. The
`PJRT_DeviceEvent` signals when the access is established, `vtable->get_info`
reads `(fd, offset, size)`, and `vtable->destroy` ends the access. When client
and plugin live in the same binary, the client unwraps the underlying
`AsyncValue` directly with no extra allocation. `PjRtCApiRawBuffer` also
overrides `AcquireExternalDmaAccess()` to forward through the wrapped C raw
buffer.

display_title: [IFRT] Remove redundant `DCHECK(this)` checks in IFRT and PjRt-IFRT

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Remove redundant `DCHECK(this)` checks in IFRT and PjRt-IFRT

In C++, invoking a non-static member function on a null pointer is undefined behavior before the function body executes, allowing compilers to assume `this` is always non-null. As a result, `DCHECK(this)` inside member functions provides no reliable runtime protection and serves only as dead boilerplate.

Remove all remaining `DCHECK(this)` assertions across `xla::ifrt::Sharding`, `xla::ifrt::ShardingSpec`, IFRT IR loaded executables, and PjRt-IFRT client, array, executable, compiler, tuple, and string-array implementations. Also prune the resulting unused includes and build dependencies.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017806314

display_title: PR #129734: Add tf.experimental.numpy diff prepend/append support with NumPy semantics

head_commit.message:
PR #129734: Add tf.experimental.numpy diff prepend/append support with NumPy semantics

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/pull/129734

NumPy's `np.diff` accepts optional `prepend`/`append` values that are added along `axis` before the differences run:

```
>>> np.diff(np.array([1, 2, 3]), prepend=0)
array([1, 1, 1])

>>> np.diff(np.array([1, 2, 3]), append=5)
array([1, 1, 2])
```

The tf-numpy wrapper lacked both parameters entirely: `tnp.diff(a, prepend=0)` raises `TypeError: diff() got an unexpected keyword argument 'prepend'`.

Mirror NumPy's implementation in `np_math_ops.diff`:

- A scalar (0-d) `prepend`/`append` is broadcast to length 1 along `axis` and all other dimensions of `a` (NumPy's `_broadcast_to` on `shape` with `shape[axis] = 1`) and concatenated once, before the `n` differences run.
- An array `prepend`/`append` is concatenated as-is; when both shapes are statically known, a dimension mismatch outside `axis` raises NumPy's exact `ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly` instead of the backend's `InvalidArgumentError`.
- The two sides are promoted to a shared dtype with `np_utils.result_type` before concatenating, like NumPy's concatenate promotes (e.g. `np.diff(int32, prepend=1.5)` yields float64).
- Boolean inputs keep the boolean (`!=`) difference semantics when the promoted dtype is still boolean.

Tests extend `testDiff`: scalar `prepend`/`append` (including `n=2` with both boundaries), array `prepend` with `axis=0` and array `append` with `axis=1` matched against `np.diff`, the mixed-dtype promotion case, the boolean-boundary case, and a mismatch outside `axis` raising NumPy's ValueError.

Signed-off-by: Kaivalya Singh <singh.kaivalya@gmail.com>

Copybara import of the project:

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Merge PhasedBlockClusterFusion into ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion.

The two emitters are sharing a lot of code already and there are some detail leaking from PhasedBlockCluster emitter to make it horizontally fuseable, so it makes more sense to have a generic emission pipeline.

* HLO fusions can be annotated with both `__thread_block_specialized` and `__phased_block_cluster` fusion kinds to indicate scheduling decisions.
* Emitter supports arbitrary nesting of fusions.

display_title: [TF] Switch TensorFlow default build to Bzlmod and sync MODULE.bazel.

head_commit.message:
[TF] Switch TensorFlow default build to Bzlmod and sync MODULE.bazel.

Following the Bazel 8.8.2 upgrade, enable `--enable_bzlmod` and `--noenable_workspace` by default in TensorFlow while adding `--config=workspace` as a fallback configuration and flipping `ci/official/envs/bzlmod` to `--config workspace` so `WORKSPACE` continues to be tested in CI for downstream consumers. Also set `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5` and `common --experimental_downloader_config=bazel_downloader.cfg` (including BCR mirror fallback rules), add `--nobuild_runfile_links` to `common:rbe_base`, prepend Bzlmod canonical CUDA library paths to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in `test:linux_cuda_13_wheel_test`, and disable `layering_check` on macOS (`common:macos`) to match Linux and Windows toolchains.

In `MODULE.bazel`, third-party Bzlmod extensions, and platform patches:
- Register the hermetic SYCL and ROCm C++ toolchains from `rules_ml_toolchain`, sync the CUDA, CCCL (`3.4.0`), NCCL (`nccl_redist_patched`), NVSHMEM, SYCL, local sysroot, and `libdrm` module extensions and XLA third-party repositories (including deduplicating `nccl_archive`, `nvtx_archive`, `png`, and `absl_py` from `tf_third_party`) with XLA's `MODULE.bazel` and `workspace2.bzl`, and align the root BCR module declarations (`pybind11_bazel` 3.0.0, `apple_support` 2.8.0, `rules_swift` 2.9.0, `googletest` 1.18.0, `highway` 1.4.0, `dev_dependency = True` on test-only modules `rules_webtesting`, `fuzztest`, and `libprotobuf-mutator`, and `repo_name = None` compatibility pins for `c-ares`, `eigen`, `grpc-java`, and `libpfm`).
- Configure multi-platform `pip.parse` wheels (`xla_pypi = "pypi"`, `local_wheels` overrides via `rules_python_local_wheel.patch`, `@pypi//{}:whl` in `tf_wheel.bzl`, and Python 3.14 freethreaded lockfile/platform support), `pythons_hub`, `python_version_repo` via `use_repo_rule` (with `REQUIREMENTS` lockfile support, `TF_PYTHON_VERSION` fallback, `-freethreaded`/`-ft` suffix handling, and removing the unused `python_version_ext` extension), reproducible module extensions (`reproducible = True` on `third_party_ext`, `googleapis_ext`, and `nccl_redist_ext`), `maven`, and Bzlmod Java repositories (`generated_rule_name` in `java_repos.bzl` and Guava/JSR305/ErrorProne repos), alias `@system_python//:python_headers` to `rules_python`'s hermetic headers in `bazel9.patch`, and update `nvidia_wheel_deps`, `requirements_lock_3_*.txt` (`protobuf==6.33.6`), and `code_check_full.bats` for Bzlmod.
- Add Bzlmod compatibility patch overrides (`pybind11_abseil.patch`, Windows DLL support in `protobuf/bazel9.patch`, `google_cloud_cpp.patch`, `rules_android.patch`, and `googletest:remove_alwayslink.patch`), update Windows protobuf symbol exports in `_pywrap_tensorflow.def`, and update `gpu_prim.h` and `where_op_gpu.cu.h` (`THRUST_VERSION >= 300200`) for CCCL 3.4.0 compatibility.

Follow-up CLs will clean up remaining legacy WORKSPACE artifacts and deprecated `BUILD.oss` `$(location)` make variables, migrate remaining `java_import_external` and `tf_third_party` repositories to BCR modules/`rules_jvm_external`, and re-enable Bazel 8 incompatible flags in `.bazelrc`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Stabilize short-kernel autotuning and transpose threads.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Stabilize short-kernel autotuning and transpose threads.

***Problem:*** Single-sample GPU autotuner profiling suffers from launch jitter on short kernels that misranks fusion backends, while larger CUDA packed transpose thread blocks slow wider element types due to extra shared-memory loop overhead.

***Solution:*** Repeat-sample short GPU kernels in `GpuProfiler::Profile` and report the median duration, while restricting larger CUDA `PackedTranspose` thread blocks to sub-byte and byte-wide element types.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Flush L2 and average timed runs when autotuning on GPU.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Flush L2 and average timed runs when autotuning on GPU.

***Problem:*** `GpuProfiler` times each autotuning candidate once right after a warm-up run, so operands remain L2-resident and timer quantization hides cold-cache execution differences, making config selection noisy across compilations.

***Solution:*** Overwrite a scratch buffer twice the L2 cache size before each timed run and report the mean across `xla_gpu_autotune_num_timed_runs` timed runs when autotuning is enabled and `xla_gpu_autotune_flush_l2_cache` is set.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Scale Triton fusion warps up to 16 and 32 for large tiles.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Scale Triton fusion warps up to 16 and 32 for large tiles.

***Problem:*** `EstimateNumWarps` caps every Triton fusion at 8 warps regardless of register pressure, causing non-dot fusions with large live tiles, multiple wide reductions, or wide epilogue inputs alongside a reduction to drop to single-block SM residency or spill registers.

***Solution:*** Scale non-dot Triton fusions to 16 or 32 warps when live tile sizes, cumulative reduced elements, or independent wide epilogue inputs exceed single-block register thresholds, while keeping dot fusions capped at 8 warps and clamping to the target device's threads-per-block limit.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Optimize packed transpose codegen and vector alignment.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Optimize packed transpose codegen and vector alignment.

***Problem:*** Unaligned vector transfer lowering and scalar elementwise shared-memory extraction split 32-bit packed loads and stores into narrow memory operations, inflate sub-byte vector SelectionDAG legalization, and under-occupy packed transpose blocks.

***Solution:*** Infer byte alignment from base buffers and affine index divisors, lower aligned power-of-two sub-byte vector transfers through wide integer loads and stores, and transpose 32-bit packed shared-memory tiles with an in-register `i32` butterfly at 256 threads per block.

head_commit.message:
Update TPU_8T default VMEM limit to 64 MiB in PlatformInfo.

`PlatformInfo` for `TPU_8T` previously set `default_vmem_limit_kib` to 32 MiB (`32 * 1024` KiB), causing Pallas microbenchmarks and cost models to select tile sizes assuming a 32 MiB budget even though the kernel compiled and ran under the XLA HLO compiler's 64 MiB default scoped VMEM limit.

Update `default_vmem_limit_kib` for `TPU_8T` in `xla/benchmarks/core/platform_info.py` to `64 * 1024` KiB (64 MiB) for parity with the XLA HLO default, so callers of `get_default_vmem_limit_kib` select window sizes against the same 64 MiB budget used by XLA when `--xla_tpu_scoped_vmem_limit_kib` is unset.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Linearize small staged async H2D transfers inline in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Linearize small staged async H2D transfers inline in CommonPjRtClient.

For `kImmutableUntilTransferCompletes` transfers, `LinearizeIntoImpl` always
dispatched the linearize + H2D copy to `async_work_runner()`, even when the
staging buffer was already available. That extra thread hop per tensor
exposes multi-host synchronous steps to work-queue tail latency.

Run linearization inline when the buffer is <= 512 KiB and the staging buffer
is already available; larger or throttled transfers still go through
`async_work_runner()`.

Measured on a 256-chip TPU training job (8 input tensors, 264 KiB per chip per
step), together with a companion change in the Pathways transport layer:
stalls >= 25s went from 11 in 4,200 steps (max 118s) to 0, and steady-state
throughput went from ~105 to ~145 steps/min (+30-40%).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017694836

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Stabilize short-kernel autotuning and transpose threads.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Stabilize short-kernel autotuning and transpose threads.

***Problem:*** Single-sample GPU autotuner profiling suffers from launch jitter on short kernels that misranks fusion backends, while larger CUDA packed transpose thread blocks slow wider element types due to extra shared-memory loop overhead.

***Solution:*** Repeat-sample short GPU kernels in `GpuProfiler::Profile` and report the median duration, while restricting larger CUDA `PackedTranspose` thread blocks to sub-byte and byte-wide element types.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Optimize packed transpose codegen and vector alignment.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Optimize packed transpose codegen and vector alignment.

***Problem:*** Unaligned vector transfer lowering and scalar elementwise shared-memory extraction split 32-bit packed loads and stores into narrow memory operations, inflate sub-byte vector SelectionDAG legalization, and under-occupy packed transpose blocks.

***Solution:*** Infer byte alignment from base buffers and affine index divisors, lower aligned power-of-two sub-byte vector transfers through wide integer loads and stores, and transpose 32-bit packed shared-memory tiles with an in-register `i32` butterfly at 256 threads per block.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1015328781

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Flush L2 and average timed runs when autotuning on GPU.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Flush L2 and average timed runs when autotuning on GPU.

***Problem:*** `GpuProfiler` times each autotuning candidate once right after a warm-up run, so operands remain L2-resident and timer quantization hides cold-cache execution differences, making config selection noisy across compilations.

***Solution:*** Overwrite a scratch buffer twice the L2 cache size before each timed run and report the mean across `xla_gpu_autotune_num_timed_runs` timed runs when autotuning is enabled and `xla_gpu_autotune_flush_l2_cache` is set.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Scale Triton fusion warps up to 16 and 32 for large tiles.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Scale Triton fusion warps up to 16 and 32 for large tiles.

***Problem:*** `EstimateNumWarps` caps every Triton fusion at 8 warps regardless of register pressure, causing non-dot fusions with large live tiles, multiple wide reductions, or wide epilogue inputs alongside a reduction to drop to single-block SM residency or spill registers.

***Solution:*** Scale non-dot Triton fusions to 16 or 32 warps when live tile sizes, cumulative reduced elements, or independent wide epilogue inputs exceed single-block register thresholds, while keeping dot fusions capped at 8 warps and clamping to the target device's threads-per-block limit.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use collective memory space for temporary buffers on fully-sharded modules.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use collective memory space for temporary buffers on fully-sharded modules.

When temporary buffers are allocated on `BFCAllocator`, other allocations can shift the temporary buffer address across executions and trigger expensive CUDA Graph updates.

Add `--xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_collective_color` to allocate temporary buffers for fully-sharded modules in the collective memory space, keeping their addresses stable across runs. Also fix `BufferAssignment::CombineTempAllocations` to apply `temp_buffer_color` when there is only a single default-colored temporary allocation.

Placing temp buffer in collective memory space for fully-shared module is safe because temp buffer is symmetrical across all peers.

The only side-affect of this change is that it's enabling NCCL RMA kernels if they are using temp default buffers. However currently NCCL RMA kernels are disabled by default.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017630114

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Complete synchronous executions before returning.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Complete synchronous executions before returning.

PjRt-IFRT runs programs with host callbacks synchronously. On CPU, a single
device synchronous execution now waits for its dependencies on the calling
thread instead of running asynchronously, Execute waits for a multi device
one, and neither takes a pacing reservation. Dispatches from inside a host
callback skip both waits.
This fixes a deadlock where computations queued behind a program with host
callbacks held every reservation while executions started by its callbacks
waited for one, as in Pallas TPU interpret mode's thread_map.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017622518

head_commit.message:
Add `TraceMeFilter::kTraceHostEnqueueCallback = 1` in `trace_filter_utils.h`, and clear that bit (bit 1, mask `0x2`) in `kTraceMeDefaultFilterMask` in `traceme.h` using a new `kTraceMeHostEnqueueCallbackFilter` constant with the same value. `traceme.h` cannot depend on `trace_filter_utils.h`, so `traceme_recorder_test` checks with a `static_assert` that the two stay equal.

Sessions configured with `host_traceme_filter_mask = (1ULL << kTraceHostEnqueueCallback)` record only `TraceMe` events tagged with that bit. Sessions without a filter or with the `kTraceMemory` filter record the same events as before, including the tagged ones. `traceme_recorder_test` covers both cases.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Complete synchronous executions before returning.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Complete synchronous executions before returning.

PjRt-IFRT runs programs with host callbacks synchronously. On CPU, a single
device synchronous execution now waits for its dependencies on the calling
thread instead of running asynchronously, Execute waits for a multi device
one, and neither takes a pacing reservation. Dispatches from inside a host
callback skip both waits.
This fixes a deadlock where computations queued behind a program with host
callbacks held every reservation while executions started by its callbacks
waited for one, as in Pallas TPU interpret mode's thread_map.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 996035135

display_title: PR #52024: [XLA] Include frontend attributes in DotMerger's merge key

head_commit.message:
PR #52024: [XLA] Include frontend attributes in DotMerger's merge key

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52024

:pencil: **Summary of Changes**

Include frontend attributes in `DotMerger`'s merge equivalence key, as sorted (key, value) pairs (not a joined string, so different maps can never produce the same key). Dots with different frontend attributes are no longer merged.

:dart: **Justification**

Frontend attributes are the mechanism by which the frontend (e.g. JAX) attaches annotations to HLO instructions for downstream passes to consume. A merged dot can carry only one attribute map, so merging two dots with different annotations silently drops one of them. `DotMerger` was not accounting for this, so annotated matmuls lost their scheduling annotations when merged.

:compass: **Design: why `DotMerger` refuses to merge dots whose attributes differ**

A merged dot can carry only one attribute map, so the options are to refuse the merge, to keep one map (dropping the other dot's annotation, which is the bug this MR fixes), or to union the values. Union is what the collective combiners do for attributes that are not merge boundaries (`MergeFrontendAttributes` joins different values with `","`), but for annotations like `_scheduling_group_id` that produces an invalid value, and `LegalizeSchedulingAnnotations` already treats two different scheduling annotations inside one fusion as an error. Refusing is consistent with existing merge boundaries:

| Existing code | Boundary | Key encoding |
|---|---|---|
| GPU all-gather / all-reduce / reduce-scatter combiners (`AppendFrontendAttributesToCombinerKey`, openxla/xla#46097) | `collective_group_key`, `combiner_key`; an annotated op never combines with an unannotated one | length-prefixed, "so arbitrary frontend strings cannot produce colliding combiner keys" |
| `CollectivePermuteKey` (same PR) | same two attributes | separate struct fields |
| `DotMerger` on GPU (`queue_id`, openxla/xla#17999) | dots on different streams | integer field in the same `EquivalenceKey` |

Here the attributes are user annotations with arbitrary keys (e.g. `set_xla_metadata(layer="L1")`), so the whole map is the boundary. In unannotated programs this changes nothing: XLA itself attaches frontend attributes to collectives and loops but not to dots (checked on DeepSeek-V3 MaxText HLO: 0 of 48 dots carry any), so merges are only skipped where the user annotated dots differently.

:rocket: **Kind of Contribution**

:bug: Bug Fix

:test_tube: **Unit Tests:**

Added hardware-independent tests asserting frontend attributes survive dot merging:

* `dot_merger_test.cc`:
  * `MergedDotKeepsIdenticalFrontendAttributes`: verifies dots with matching attributes merge into one carrying them.
  * `NoMergeAcrossDifferentFrontendAttributes`: verifies dots with different attributes are never merged.
  * `NoMergeOfTaggedAndUntaggedDots`: verifies a tagged and an untagged dot are never merged.
  * `NoMergeOfDifferentFrontendAttributesWithSameRendering`: verifies `{a: "b;c=d"}` and `{a: "b", c: "d"}`, which a joined `key=value;...` key would conflate, are never merged.

:test_tube: **Execution Tests:**

No new checked-in execution test was added.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce support and fix reduce lowering

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Forbid parameter-only reducers in Triton reduce lowering

The lanes past the end of a tile are masked with the reduction's init value,
which assumes that the init value is a neutral element of the combiner. A
combiner that just returns one of its parameters, e.g. the `(a, b) -> b`
combiner of a "take last" reduction, has no such neutral value: every padded
reduction dimension silently returned the init value instead of the last
element.

Forbid these computations in CanTritonHandleReduce so the fusion falls back to
the native emitter, which handles them correctly.

While here:
- EmitCombinerStep passed an empty instruction list to EmitScope, which reads
  `instructions.back()`, so loop-tiled parameter-only reducers crashed. Handle
  the empty case explicitly; the Xtile emitter is also used by the CPU backend,
  so it keeps supporting these combiners.
- Hoist `TensorValue result` in EmitReduceComputation so that the terminator is
  emitted once instead of duplicating the ReturnOp and the insertion point.
- Add regression tests: a parameter-only reducer with a non-neutral init value
  pins down the accumulator/element argument mapping in LowerReduce, and a
  loop-tiled "take last" case covers the empty to_emit path.
